newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Makhteshim buys Brazilian firm.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Makhteshim buys Brazilian firm.

text.p: Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd and its Agan Chemicals Manufacturers Ltd subsidiary said on Monday they had acquired 83 percent of a Brazilian agro-chemicals company for $19.8 million.

The purchase of Brazil's Defenpar Participacoes from a group of agricultural cooperatives and private investors is the latest in a string of foreign acquisitions by the two Israeli companies, the world's largest manufacturers of generic herbicides and pesticides.

Defenpar, based in Brazil's southern state of Taquari, had sales of $80 million in 1995, about 30 percent of them exports. It manufactures and markets crop-protection chemicals, intermediate agro-chemicals, veterinary products and other chemicals.

Like Makhteshim group's other acquisitions in recent months, Defenpar has an established relationship with the Israeli companies and is their second-largest customer in Latin America, Makhteshim said. Agan buys intermediate products from Defenpar.

Yehuda Milo, Makhteshim's chairman, said the three recent acquisitions would generate additional revenues of $200-250 million, compared with consolidated 1995 sales for Makhteshim of approximately $480 million.

In recent months, Makhteshim and Agan have acquired 49 percent stakes in Herbitechnica, another Brazilian agro-chemicals concern, and in a Spanish company Aragonesas as well as the assets of an Argentinian company.
Makhteshim is 67 percent-owned by Koor Industries .
The remaining shares in Defenpar will be held by the company's senior managers.
